panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: The image is a CT scan of a patient showing the anatomy of the anomalous coronary artery with an intramural course, as stated in the caption and supported by the title. It is a diagnostic image. B: The image is a CT scan of a patient showing the anatomy of the anomalous coronary artery with an intramural course. It is a diagnostic image. C: The image is a CT scan specifically demonstrating the key measurement (commissure-intramural distance) related to the diagnosis and treatment planning for the anomalous coronary artery with intramural course. D: The image is a 3D CT reconstruction of a patient, used to illustrate the anatomical relationship of the anomalous coronary artery, which is central to the study's findings.

Multiplanar reformatted (MPR) enhanced CT images demonstrating measurement of the commissure-intramural distance. (A) Axial view. (B) Sagittal view. (C) Coronal view used for measurement of the shortest distance between the superior edge of the aortic commissure and the intramural segment of the anomalous coronary artery (double-headed arrow). The double-headed arrow in panel D represents the same commissure-intramural distance measured on the coronal MPR image shown in panel C.

A: Panel A is a CT angiography showing the long and trifurcated left main coronary artery with a prepulmonic course, directly supporting the diagnosis of AAOCA. B: Panel B is coronary angiography demonstrating the anomalous origin of the left main coronary artery. C: Panel C is coronary angiography supporting the overall clinical presentation of AAOCA.

The scintigraphy with sestamibi showed myocardial ischemia of a small-to-moderate area, involving parts of the apical region and inferoapical and inferior regions of the left ventricle. Invasive stratification performed with coronary angiography showed the anomalous aortic origin of the left main coronary artery at the right semilunar cusp of the aortic valve. The CT angiography showed a long and trifurcated left main coronary artery, with a prepulmonic course (Figure 2). Once again, this AAOCA pattern was not recognized as potentially serious, and the patient was discharged asymptomatic.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an echocardiogram showing the right coronary artery originating from the left coronary sinus, with an acute angle of takeoff and an intramural course, consistent with AAOCA. B: Panel B is an echocardiogram showing the left coronary artery and its branches with slender luminal caliber and reduced blood flow signals, indicative of hypoplastic development related to AAOCA.

panels.figure_caption: (A) the right coronary artery originates from the left coronary sinus, with an acutely angled ostium and an intramural course within the aortic wall. (B) The left coronary artery and its branches exhibit slender luminal caliber with reduced blood flow signals (marked by a green arrow).
in_text_mentions: Detailed coronary evaluation subsequently demonstrated that the right coronary artery (RCA) originated from the left coronary sinus with an acute angle of origin and an intramural aortic course (diameter: 2.3 mm). The left main coronary artery (LM) showed hypoplastic development (diameter: 1.3 mm) (Figure 3 and Supplementary Movie S4). Following interdisciplinary consultation and confirmation of anatomical abnormalities, the patient was transferred to a tertiary cardiovascular center for advanced management owing to critical clinical status, and family consent was obtained.
